findings.text: issue (blocking): The amnesty accepts an uncommitted working-tree `status: closed`, so an in-flight change with a lost plan commit can bypass the required BLOCK. The historical fallback also grants amnesty when the current intent is absent, unreadable, or malformed, contradicting the stated fail-closed boundary.
findings.fix: Require a parseable current intent and a committed closed status reachable from HEAD; otherwise return the existing no-plan-commit BLOCK, with regression tests for uncommitted closure and deleted, unreadable, and malformed current intents after historical closure.

findings.text: issue (blocking): New behavior relies on externally owned Git CLI semantics for `reset --soft`, commit creation, and ref rewriting without a grounding citation, so the claimed squash equivalence is unsupported under this lens.
findings.fix: Cite the authoritative Git documentation beside the squash implementation for the relied-upon reset, commit, and update-ref semantics.

findings.text: issue: The plan states that an unreadable intent blocks, but the implementation falls back to historical closure and can return NOT APPLICABLE.
findings.fix: Make the implementation fail closed for an unreadable current intent so this recorded risk remains true.

findings.text: issue (blocking): When the source resolves its trunk through local `main` or `master`, `trunk_remote_ref` becomes null and the following loop deletes every `origin/*` ref. The resulting squashed rehearsal lacks `origin/main`, unlike the post-squash CI checkout it promises to model, so a probe that skips when that ref is absent can falsely pass.
findings.fix: Map local `main`/`master` selections to the corresponding `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` ref and update that ref to `new_sha`; add a divergent-feature/local-trunk regression test asserting it remains reachable in the squashed run.

findings.text: issue (unfixed): The fix covers uncommitted, deleted, and malformed current intents, but still lacks the previously required regression case proving that an unreadable current intent blocks after historical closure.
findings.fix: Add a regression test that makes reading the current intent raise OSError after committing a historical closed status, then assert plan-edits returns the existing no-plan-commit BLOCK.

findings.text: issue (unfixed): The unreadable-intent regression checks only the plan.edits-after-commit rule ID, so it can pass for a different BLOCK reason and does not pin the required existing no-plan-commit BLOCK.
findings.fix: Add `assert "no plan commit found" in result.stderr` to `test_unreadable_intent_after_historical_closure_still_blocks`.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The squashed rehearsal assumes the selected trunk SHA is an ancestor of HEAD, but never verifies that assumption. If origin/main advances after the branch diverges, reset --soft keeps the feature branch's old tree and commits it on the newer trunk, deleting upstream changes instead of modeling the tree a real squash merge would produce; probes can therefore return the wrong result.
findings.fix: Before constructing the squashed shape, either require git merge-base --is-ancestor <trunk-sha> <head-sha> and fail with an actionable rebase-required message, or construct the actual merged tree; add a regression test where origin/main and the feature branch have diverged.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The branch-end dispatches are present, but probes[] contains only wave-end evidence at SHA 83d129c9; it has no adversarial or blind-run entry for reviewed SHA 3d3422f7ef1f700f0bcde3dde05330e6a6280858. The required branch-end verification therefore cannot be reproduced from the record.
findings.fix: Append the branch-end package-test, adversarial, and blind-run probe entries with their exact commands, artifacts, scope, and SHA 3d3422f7ef1f700f0bcde3dde05330e6a6280858 before accepting this checkpoint.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The executable gate tells Build that the second run models a branch squashed onto its trunk, but gives no ancestry precondition or divergence handling. A cold executor can rely on a misleading rehearsal when trunk advanced independently.
findings.fix: State and enforce in this gate that the selected trunk must be an ancestor of the rehearsed HEAD, with divergence requiring a rebase or a merge-accurate rehearsal before graduation.

findings.text: nitpick (non-blocking): The new probe uses camelCase components instead of the required test_<unit>_<state>_<expected> function-name shape.
findings.fix: Rename this probe and the other newly added camelCase probe functions to snake_case test_<unit>_<state>_<expected> names, updating the graduated copies and recorded commands together.

findings.text: issue (blocking): `parse_document` silently keeps the last of duplicate frontmatter keys, so an invalid intent containing both confirmed and closed `status:` lines can be treated as shipped and receive NOT APPLICABLE instead of the fail-closed BLOCK.
findings.fix: Reject duplicate `status:` frontmatter before granting the carve-out, and make `test_planedits_duplicatestatus_blocks` pass while retaining the existing single-status cases.

findings.text: issue (blocking): Trunk resolution accepts the first resolvable ref without validating its relationship to HEAD or conflicting same-name trunk refs; `_squash_clone_onto_trunk` then uses `reset --soft`, which can fabricate a green tree that drops newer divergent trunk content or squash from a stale base.
findings.fix: Resolve candidate refs to commits, fail loudly when the selected trunk is divergent or inconsistent with the applicable same-name trunk history, and make both `test_rehearsal_trunkbehindmergebase_failsloudly` and `test_rehearsal_trunkaheadofbranch_failsloudly` pass.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The record contains no branch-end probe entries at the reviewed SHA: all five recorded probes still name the earlier wave-end SHA and omit `scope`, despite committed branch-end adversarial and blind-run artifacts. The checkpoint therefore cannot reproduce or gate the current evidence.
findings.fix: Append the branch-end package-test, adversarial, and blind-run probe entries with their exact commands, artifacts, `scope: branch-end`, and SHA binding for this round before recording verdicts.

findings.text: issue (blocking): The report says the package-suite environment is the only missing evidence, but the already-committed branch-end adversarial catalogue exposes three failing cases, including two ways the squash rehearsal can model the wrong history. This hides known blockers at the user's acceptance point.
findings.fix: Regenerate the blind-run report after the branch-end probes and findings are recorded, explicitly listing the failing adversarial boundaries and withholding an acceptance-ready summary until they pass or are validly dismissed.
